display.purpose: Homepage hero headline and major section openers. Rare — used when type is the visual event.

headline.purpose: Section headings, case study titles, page-level headers.

title.purpose: Service names, case study structural labels (Brief, Strategy, Impact), card headings.

body.purpose: All running copy. Max 65-75ch line length. Never condensed.

label.purpose: Tags, chips, navigation links, captions, metadata, footer. Uppercase only at this scale.

shadows.name: ambient-float
shadows.purpose: Floating UI only — persistent sticky tab or element that must visually separate from the page surface. Not for cards or hover states.

motion.name: ease-out-quart
motion.purpose: Default easing for all UI state transitions. Snappy entry, relaxed exit.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Button and link hover state colour transitions.

components.name: Cutout Mask
components.description: Signature component. Solid accent surface with B&W photography revealed through geometric cutouts. The defining visual device of the system.
components.html: Look Twice.
components.css: .ds-cutout { position: relative; overflow: hidden; } .ds-cutout__text { position: absolute; top: 48px; left: 48px; z-index: 2; max-width: 50%; } .ds-cutout__heading { font-family: Epilogue, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: clamp(3rem, 7vw, 5.5rem); font-weight: 700; line-height: 1; letter-spacing: -0.02em; color: #FFFFFF; } .ds-cutout__shape { position: absolute; overflow: hidden; } .ds-cutout__shape img { width: 100%; height: 100%; object-fit: cover; filter: grayscale(100%); } .ds-cutout__shape--rect { border-radius: 16px; } .ds-cutout__shape--circle { border-radius: 50%; } .ds-cutout__shape--large { width: 45%; padding-bottom: 55%; right: 48px; top: 48px; } .ds-cutout__shape--small { width: 18%; padding-bottom: 18%; right: 44%; bottom: 48px; }

narrative.overview:
The surface is never the whole story. In this visual system, bold colour dominates the foreground - then geometric cutouts reveal what is underneath. B&W photography emerges through rounded rectangles and circles cut into solid fields of accent colour. The brand name earns its place in every layout decision: look again, something was there that was not visible at first. Restraint and revelation in the same frame.

This is a system of two modes. Hero (Cutout) mode is drenched in accent colour - one saturated hue carries 60-80% of the surface, with desaturated photography breaking through geometric apertures. Working (Colour Block) mode grounds everything on Linen, using the accent palette structurally: category chips, vertical bars, pull-quote blocks, data annotations. Both modes share one typeface, one weight contrast logic, and one photography treatment. The cohesion is the system.

What this system rejects: generic consultancy polish, luxury serif aesthetics, stock photography used carelessly, decorative gradients, glassmorphism, and identical card grids. If a layout could belong to any solo brand strategist's site, it has failed.
keyCharacteristics: Two-mode system: drenched Hero (Cutout) and structured Working (Colour Block)
Single typeface (Epilogue), maximum weight contrast — Bold or Regular, nothing between
B&W photography in hero compositions; full colour for evidence and research
Geometric cutout as the signature visual device
Colour is committed and purposeful, never ambient decoration
Flat elevation: depth through tonal contrast, not shadows

rules.name: The Commitment Rule
rules.body: Every accent surface is a deliberate choice, not a reflex. Before placing a colour, name the reason: which section, which emotional register, which moment in the user's journey needs to stop the eye here.

rules.name: The One Surface Rule
rules.body: A single accent colour occupies a hero or section opener. Two accents on one surface create noise, not energy. Gradients are the one exception: they blend adjacent accents (Pink-Orange, Purple-Indigo) but never introduce a third.

rules.name: The Midnight-or-Linen Rule
rules.body: Background is Midnight or Linen. There is no mid-tone grey in this system. Linen for working and explanatory content; Midnight for authority, transition moments, and sections that need to feel structurally distinct.

rules.name: The No Medium Rule
rules.body: Medium weight (500) is not in this system. The contrast is Bold (700) or Regular (400). A third weight muddies the hierarchy. Use one or the other.

rules.name: The Italic Exception
rules.body: Italics are for pull quotes and register shifts only — not for emphasis within body copy. Emphasis in running text uses Bold.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadows appear only when an element is genuinely floating above the page. Reaching for a shadow to make a card feel designed is a signal to redesign the card.

dos: Do use a single accent colour as the dominant surface in hero and section openers. Commit to it fully — half-committed colour reads as uncertainty.
Do desaturate or convert to B&W all photography in Cutout/Hero mode. Colour comes from the surface field. The photograph is the texture, not the statement.
Do show evidence and research photography in full natural colour — never desaturate material that must convey real-world context.
Do use Epilogue Bold (700) and Epilogue Regular (400) only. No medium weight.
Do cap body line length at 65-75ch. No full-width paragraphs.
Do check WCAG AA contrast on every surface.
Do write descriptive alt text for all images, including cutout compositions.
Do use motion to aid understanding — scroll-driven reveals, timeline animations. Not decorative transitions.
donts: Don't produce generic solo brand strategist site patterns: stock hero photo, 'We help brands grow' headline, four icon-plus-text cards in a grid.
Don't use luxury serif typography or high-polish agency aesthetics. Wrong register for the SME and scale-up audience.
Don't use identical card grids. Cards are used sparingly; grids of them never are.
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a coloured stripe on cards, callouts, or list items.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with a gradient fill). Use a solid colour.
Don't use glassmorphism except where absolutely necessary for spatial grounding.
Don't place two competing accent colours on the same surface.
Don't use decorative motion: no fade-in-from-below on every paragraph, no parallax for atmosphere.
Don't use #000000 as a background. Midnight (#26263E) is the dark surface.
Don't use mid-tone grey backgrounds. This system has Midnight and Linen. Nothing in between.
Don't use box shadows on cards or hover states. Shadows appear only on genuinely floating elements.
